en: The Scripture on the Buddha’s Entry into the Inconceivable Realm of the Tathāgata’s Virtue and Wisdom Adorned with Flowers, Volume One.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Jñānagupta of India during the Sui Dynasty.
Thus have I heard:
At one time the Bhagavān was staying in the country of Magadha, at the site of the Bodhi tree in the Dharmāranya, within the Hall of Universal Radiance;
he was the accumulation of great merit, born of wondrous joy, dwelling in a place universally beyond reproach, and possessed of immeasurable virtues.

Seated upon the lion throne within the Lotus Treasury, he is: first, one who has realized awakening with equanimity; second, one whose awakening is perfectly pure; third, one who is free from dualistic conduct;
fourth, one who traverses where the Buddhas traverse; fifth, one who has attained equality with all Buddhas;
sixth, one who has reached the realm of non-obstruction; seventh, one of the dharma of non-retrogression; eighth, one whose conduct is unimpeded; ninth, one who is... [incomplete].
9. Abandoning the activities performed by boundless Buddhas; 10. Dwelling in the inconceivable state; 11. Tending toward the signless Dharma; 12.
Arising from the equality of the three periods of time; 13. His body pervading all worlds; 14.
Being without doubt or confusion regarding the wisdom of all phenomena; 15. Possessing perfect awakening and insight regarding all spheres of practice.
5. Not being subject to deliberation or difficulty regarding the knowledge of all phenomena;
16. The non-conceptual body; 17. Receiving the wisdom of all bodhisattvas; 18. Attaining the supreme further shore of the non-dual conduct of Buddhas; 19.
Reaching the limit of the undifferentiated liberation-wisdom of the Tathāgatas; 20. Proceeding in accordance with that which is boundless and without center.
21. The equality of the Buddha-ground; 22. The ultimate limit of the dharma-realm; 23. The finality of the realm of empty space;
24. Exhausting the end of the future limit; 25. Constantly turning the wheel of Dharma throughout all kalpas without the body ever resting.
Together with six million two hundred thousand bhikṣus, namely:
first, Śāriputra (translated into Chinese as Qúyú zǐ, formerly known as Shèlìfú);
second, Mahāmaudgalyāyana (formerly known as Dàmùqiélián); and third, Mahākāśyapa.
1. Pāṃśu; 2. Aniruddha; 3. Subhūti (translated in the Sui dynasty as "Good Reality," formerly known as Subhūti);
4. Kātyāyana (formerly known as Kātyāyana); 5. Mahākapphiṇa (formerly known as Kapphiṇa); 6. Revata; 7. Nanda.
10. Nadīkāśyapa; 11. Gayākāśyapa; 12. Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra (translated into Chinese as Mǎn cí zǐ, formerly known as Fúlóunà);
13. Gavāmpati (translated into Chinese as Niú zhǔ, formerly known as Qiáofàn bōtí).
14. Cūḍapanthaka (translated in the Sui as "Tufted Path"; formerly known as Zhōulìpántuó); 15.
Dravyamāṇavaka (translated in the Sui as "Son of a Wealthy Man";
formerly known as Dá pó móluózǐ); 16. Khadiravaṇika; 17. Cchanda.

18. Mahākauṣṭhila; 19. Rāhula; 20. Ānanda—headed by these, there were six million two hundred thousand bhikṣus, all of whom practiced the single Dharma, equally entered the sphere of reality, all entered the practice of the self-nature of all phenomena, and all dwelt nowhere within the realm of space.
They all roam throughout the realms without relying on any fixed location; they have all already abandoned that which arises from the hindrances and coverings of afflictions;
they have all entered the luminous practice of the Dharma-realm of all Tathāgatas; they have all equally entered the single Dharma; they are all directed toward universal wisdom;
they never cease in their progress upon the path of universal wisdom; and they all proclaim the wisdom of universal wisdom.
Those who possessed regressive thoughts had all already attained the supreme other shore through the contemplation of distinct wisdom-knowledge;
they were all born from the sphere of activity of skillful means.
Furthermore, there were sixty hundred thousand bhikṣuṇīs with them:

The bhikṣuṇī Mahāprajāpatī, with Yaśodharā bhikṣuṇī at their head, had all perfectly gathered the dharmas of purity; all were close to the wisdom of universal gnosis; all had entered the practice of the light of universal gnosis; all were established in the luminous Dharma. Thus they were skillfully proficient in the signlessness of all dharmas; thus they descended into the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi) of all dharmas; thus they accorded with the non-arising and non-ceasing of all dharmas, which are without opposition or counterpart. With such faith and understanding, they all dwelt securely in the samādhi of inconceivable liberation, and they all manifested for the purpose of transforming and delivering sentient beings through the display of physical forms, classes, and dignified deportment that are effortless and non-conceptual.

Furthermore, he was accompanied by a great assembly of bodhisattvas—bodhisattva-mahāsattvas as numerous as the atoms in ten unspeakably many koṭis of nayutas of hundreds of thousands of buddha-fields.
They were as follows: the bodhisattva-mahāsattva Samantabhadra, Samantaravi, Samantavikurvita, Samantajñāna, Samantalocana, Samantaprabha, Samantāvabhāsa, and Samantapratibhāsa.
The Bodhisattva, the Bodhisattva Universal Banner, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Universal Intention,
the Bodhisattva Great Swift Movement, the Bodhisattva Great Swift Retention, the Bodhisattva Great Play, the Bodhisattva King of Great Play,
the Bodhisattva Great Vigor and Valiant Stride, the Bodhisattva Great Valiant Stride and Prowess, and the Bodhisattva Great Yawning.
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Great Yawning Power, the Bodhisattva Lord of the Great Assembly,
the Bodhisattva Moon of Equal Radiance, the Bodhisattva Stainless Moon of Dharma, the Bodhisattva Resplendent Moon, the Bodhisattva Thundering Sound Moon,
the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Moon Emitting Light, the Bodhisattva Brahma-Sound, and the Bodhisattva Brahma-Lord Thunder-Voice.
The Bodhisattvas: Earth-Resonance Sound Bodhisattva, Supreme Sound of All Sounds Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, Universal Conception Bodhisattva,
Universal Stainless Conception Bodhisattva, Virtue Conception Bodhisattva, Radiant Conception Bodhisattva, Jewel Conception Bodhisattva,
Moon Conception Bodhisattva, Sun Conception Bodhisattva, and Blazing [Conception] Bodhisattva.
Furthermore, there were the Bodhisattvas: Padmagarbha Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, Maticitra Bodhisattva,
Mahāmati Bodhisattva, Sumati Bodhisattva, Ghoṣamati Bodhisattva, Uttaramati Bodhisattva, Suvimalamati Bodhisattva,
Vardhamānamati Bodhisattva, Anantamati Bodhisattva, and Vipulamati Bodhisattva.
The Bodhisattva Awakening-Mind, the Bodhisattva Inexhaustible-Mind, the Mahāsattva Ocean-Mind, the Bodhisattva Merudīpa,
the Bodhisattva Dharmolkādīpa, the Bodhisattva Samantadigvyāpidīpa, the Bodhisattva Samantaprabhādīpa,
the Bodhisattva Sarvatamopagatadīpa, the Bodhisattva Sarvagatyudyotadīpa, and the Bodhisattva Ekānta...
The Bodhisattva Illuminating Lamp, the Bodhisattva Moon Lamp, the Mahāsattva Sun Lamp,
the Youthful Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta,
the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha, the Bodhisattva Guṇagarbha, the Bodhisattva Abandoning Evil Realms, and the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja.
Sākyamuni, Bhaiṣajyarāja Bodhisattva, Ghaṇṭāghoṣa Bodhisattva, Padmapāṇi Bodhisattva,
Sūryaprabha Bodhisattva, Virajo-vikramin Bodhisattva, Vajramati Bodhisattva,
Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin Bodhisattva, Mārajit Bodhisattva, Ratnaśikhin Bodhisattva, and the tenth...
The Bodhisattva Blazing with a Hundred Rays of Light, the Bodhisattva Great Subduer of Māras, the Bodhisattva Hard to Manifest, the Bodhisattva Hard to Subdue,
the Bodhisattva Who Has Entered the Degrees, the Bodhisattva Whose Intentions and Deeds are Hard to Praise,
the Bodhisattva Who Exhausts the Evil Realms, and the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Compassionate One— these were the leaders.
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas as numerous as the atoms in ten unspeakably many hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of Buddha-fields—
all of whom were in their final birth before Buddhahood— had gathered from various worlds. They had been well-established in the bodhisattva path,
desiring to bring to maturity the practice of skillful means through contemplation, and to transform and deliver the realms of all sentient beings.
1. To bring one being to maturity, they universally pervade all worlds; 2. through the wisdom of contemplative practice, they universally enter [all realms]; 3.

through the wisdom of contemplating and thoroughly examining the sphere of the stage of nirvāṇa; 4. through skillfully gathering the realm of sentient beings, severing all conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*), and abandoning grasping at conditioned formations;
5. through skillfully abiding in and entering the practice of the infinite Middle Way—all of these...
Sixth, they contemplate and skillfully observe that the karmic retributions of sentient beings are neither lost nor obtained;
seventh, they contemplate and skillfully observe the realm of sentient beings, giving rise to the faculty of faith and the most excellent skillful means;
eighth, they skillfully and impartially maintain, receive, and uphold the meanings, phrases, and expressions taught by all Tathāgatas of the past, future, and present through their wisdom.
9. All are well-established in entering the boundless dharmas of worldly and world-transcending practice;
10. All are well-observing the dharmas of the three times that transcend the limits of the conditioned and the unconditioned;
11. All successively and without interruption attain entry into the characteristics of the wisdom-fields of all Tathāgatas of the past, future, and present. All, in...
In every moment of mind, from moment to moment, he skillfully manifests twelve deeds:

descending into the womb, birth, renunciation, ascetic practice, proceeding to the site of enlightenment through skillful means, subduing Māra, realizing perfect awakening, turning the wheel of Dharma, and entering great parinirvāṇa;
yet in all these, he never departs from sentient beings, causing them to resolve their minds toward awakening and realize it.

13. Awakening to bodhi, all enter the mental engagement of a single sentient being’s mind in accordance with what is wholesome, reaching the mental engagement of the minds of all sentient beings without exception;
14. All abide in the naturally established ground of the immovable Bodhisattva body;
15. All attain the non-retrogressive practice of the stage of universal wisdom; 16. All enter the power of the Bodhisattva’s activities.

Seventeenth, they all practice the conduct of non-ceasing, effortless wisdom; eighteenth, they all skillfully abide in and uphold the boundless eons-long practices performed for even a single sentient being;
nineteenth, they all skillfully enter and turn the wheel of Dharma without error, abiding securely within all worlds to transform and deliver realms of beings;
and they are all fully endowed with the qualities of all Tathāgatas of the past, future, and present.
20. The power of receiving and practicing [the teachings] in pure places; 21. Possessing the supreme pure faith in all the practices and vows of Samantabhadra;
22. Visiting all the birthplaces of the Buddhas and being skillful in making requests for their teaching;
23. Skillfully upholding the Dharma-teachings of all Tathāgatas; 24. Ensuring that the lineage of all Buddhas is never interrupted.
14. All manifest the appearance of a Buddha in worlds where no Buddha exists;
15. All are able to purify turbid and defiled worlds; 16. All extinguish the karmic obstacles of all bodhisattvas;
17. All have already entered the unimpeded dharma-realm; 18. All are fully endowed with dharmas equal in measure to the realm of empty space.
19. All are fully endowed with the unimpeded equality of the dharma-realm; 30. All are fully endowed with the equality of the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) and the dharma-realm;
31. All have faith and understanding in the retributive fruits arising from the karma of majestic deportment;
32. All have faith and understanding in how effects arise according to their causes; 33. All are fully endowed with the seal and the arising of the individual seals.
34. They possess the wisdom of the equality of all phenomena; 35. They are fully endowed with the equality of phenomena, which is like a reflection in water or the moon in the sky;
36. They are fully endowed with the awakening to the resonance of all phenomena as being like echoes;
37. They all dwell securely in the inconceivable liberation-samādhi; 38. They sport freely in the Śūraṅgama-samādhi.
38. All are securely established in the *dhāraṇī* for the accomplishment and manifestation of the infinite colors of the Buddha-body;
39. All are skilled in manifesting all worlds within the path of a single hair-pore; 40.
According to the Sanskrit original, there are three phrases here that follow the sequence of the three preceding phrases [numbers] twenty, twenty-one, and twenty-two.
Because they are similar, they are not repeated; all [these deeds] are skillfully manifested within a single hair-path:

descending and being born, leaving home, practicing austerities, proceeding by skillful means to the site of enlightenment, manifesting the subduing of Māra, realizing bodhi, turning the wheel of Dharma, and entering great parinirvāṇa—these forty [deeds].
41. All possess the wisdom that, by means of a single paryanka (cross-legged posture), fills all worlds throughout the ten directions;

42. All skillfully manifest the ornaments of all lands within a single land; 43. All skillfully manifest the ornaments of a single land within all lands; 44. All skillfully manifest [the filling of... [Note:

The final term "滿" (mǎn) appears to be an incomplete fragment of a longer compound, likely *pūrṇa* or *paripūrṇa*, meaning "full" or "complete," which would correspond to the structure of the preceding items.]
45. Skillfully manifesting the assemblies of all Tathāgatas in the ten directions within a single assembly of a Tathāgata; 46.
Skillfully manifesting a single assembly of a Tathāgata within the assemblies of all Tathāgatas in the worlds of the ten directions;
47. Skillfully manifesting the bodies of all sentient beings; 48. Skillfully manifesting the bodies of all Buddhas entering into a single Buddha.
Forty-eight: skillfully manifesting forty-eight bodies; forty-nine: skillfully manifesting the body of one Buddha entering the bodies of all Buddhas; fifty:
skillfully manifesting all directions and all worlds entering within one's own body; fifty-one:
skillfully manifesting the bodies of all sentient beings of the three periods of time within the body of a single sentient being; [fifty-two: skillfully manifesting the past entering the future.
Fifty-two: entering the past from the present and future; entering the present from the past;
entering the past from the present; and entering the future from the past. Fifty-three:
skillfully entering samādhi with a single body and arising as immeasurable and innumerable bodies; skillfully...
54) Entering samādhi with immeasurable and innumerable bodies and arising from it within a single body;
55) skillfully manifesting all bodily metaphors for the realization of awakening within a single body;
56) skillfully manifesting the bodies of all sentient beings within the body of a single sentient being; [skillfully manifesting] the body of a single sentient being within all [sentient beings].
57. Skillfully manifesting the bodies of all sentient beings within one's own body; 58. Skillfully manifesting the body of one Buddha within the bodies of all Buddhas;
59. Skillfully manifesting the body of one Buddha within the bodies of all Buddhas;
60. Skillfully manifesting that the bodies of all sentient beings are themselves the Dharma-body; and skillfully manifesting the adornments of all lands.
61. Possessing the adornments of a single buddha-field within one [buddha-field]; 62. Skillfully manifesting the adornments of all buddha-fields within a single buddha-field;

63. Skillfully containing all worlds of the ten directions within a single pore, and skillfully manifesting for all sentient beings the vows, powers, and wisdom through which all Buddhas realize awakening.

Sixty-four: They have all realized enlightenment throughout the worlds of the ten directions, manifesting according to the beings they bring to maturity and those they transform, just as the Unsurpassed Perfectly Enlightened One is skillfully able to manifest; sixty-five:

they are all skillfully able to manifest the practices of a bodhisattva within every single world throughout all kalpas, their bodies never resting; sixty-six: [they are skillfully able to manifest... (as above).

At the very moment a single thought arises, throughout every world in the ten directions, for all sentient beings—whether born from eggs, born from wombs, born from moisture, or born by transformation;
whether possessing form or formless; whether with perception or without perception; whether two-legged or four-legged—[all are encompassed].
Whether they have two feet or many feet— be they devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas,
asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, śakras, brahmās, lokapālas, humans,
non-humans, and so forth— he brings them to maturity and delivers them according to their needs.
67. Thus, they skillfully manifest the sixty-seven modes of conduct, such as entering their dwellings with effortless and non-conceptual deportment;
68. they skillfully contain within a single atom immeasurable, innumerable, incomparable, unfathomable, and ineffable worlds, yet their minds remain free from distress. All of these...
He was skillful in dwelling for sixty-nine [kalpas] during a single *muhūrta* period— throughout immeasurable, innumerable, inconceivable, incomparable, unfathomable, and ineffable eons—
and he was skillful in [dwelling for] one *muhūrta* period within those immeasurable, innumerable, inconceivable, incomparable, unfathomable, and ineffable [eons].
Seventy [Bodhisattvas] abide for incalculable, immeasurable, and ineffable eons;
all of them, according to the conduct of sentient beings to be matured, are able to skillfully manifest such effortless, non-conceptual physical forms, types, and dignified postures.
Such are the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, endowed with these and other immeasurable, innumerable, koṭis, nayutas, hundreds of thousands of merits.

Furthermore, there were immeasurable, innumerable, inconceivable, incomparable, unfathomable, and ineffable numbers of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, śakras, brahmās, and world-protectors, each coming from various buddha-fields to assemble in this world-system. There were hundreds of koṭis of deities of the Cāturmahārājika heaven, each surrounded by a vast retinue, who approached the place where the Buddha was, desiring to pay homage, make offerings, serve him personally, and listen to the Dharma.

Furthermore, there were one hundred koṭis of Śakras, one hundred koṭis of Suyāma kings, one hundred koṭis of Tuṣita kings, one hundred koṭis of Sunirmita kings, and one hundred koṭis of Paranirmita-vaśavartin kings. Each of these kings was surrounded by a vast retinue as they approached the place where the Buddha was, desiring to pay their respects, make offerings, serve him personally, and listen to the Dharma.

Furthermore, there were koṭis of Māra-body devas; the merchant leader went forward to the place where the Buddha was, desiring to pay homage, make offerings, serve him personally, and listen to the Dharma.

Furthermore, there were one hundred koṭis of Brahmas, one hundred koṭis of Mahābrahmas, one hundred koṭis of Parīttābhas, one hundred koṭis of Apramāṇābhas, one hundred koṭis of Ābhāsvaras, one hundred koṭis of Parīttaśubhas, one hundred koṭis of Apramāṇaśubhas, one hundred koṭis of Śubhakṛtsnas, one hundred koṭis of Bṛhatphalas, one hundred koṭis of Sudṛśas, one hundred koṭis of Sudarśanas, one hundred koṭis of Atapas, and one hundred koṭis of Akaniṣṭha devas. Each Brahma was surrounded by a vast retinue of attendants as they approached the place where the Buddha was, desiring to pay homage, make offerings, serve him personally, and listen to the Dharma.

A hundred koṭis of devas from the Śuddhāvāsa heavens, with the son of Maheśvara as their leader, proceeded toward the place where the Buddha was, desiring to pay homage, behold him, make offerings, serve him personally, and listen to the Dharma.

A hundred koṭis of nāga lords, a hundred koṭis of yakṣa lords, a hundred koṭis of gandharva lords, a hundred koṭis of asura lords, a hundred koṭis of kinnara lords, a hundred koṭis of garuḍa lords, and a hundred koṭis of mahoraga lords—each surrounded by a vast retinue—approached the place where the Buddha was, desiring to pay homage, offer worship, serve him personally, and listen to the Dharma.

Furthermore, there were immeasurable and innumerable humans and non-humans who approached the place where the Buddha was, desiring to pay homage, make offerings, serve him personally, and listen to the Dharma.

Additionally, many hundreds of thousands of koṭis and nayutas of upāsakas and upāsikās approached the place where the Buddha was, desiring to pay homage, make offerings, serve him personally, and listen to the Dharma.

Furthermore, various medicinal herbs, forests, devas, and others—including Meru and Mahāmeru, Mucilinda and Mahāmucilinda, Himavat, Cakravāḍa, and all the mountain deities—approached the place where the Buddha was, desiring to pay homage, behold him, make offerings, serve him personally, and listen to the Dharma.

Furthermore, there were oceans, great oceans, rivers, ponds, marshes, celestial beings, and others who approached the Buddha’s dwelling, desiring to pay their respects, make offerings, serve him personally, and listen to the Dharma.

Furthermore, there were villages, cities, and royal capitals where gods and others resided; they approached the Buddha’s dwelling out of a desire to pay homage, make offerings, serve him personally, and listen to the Dharma.

Furthermore, there were devas from the palaces of the nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, kinnaras, garuḍas, and mahoragas who approached the Buddha’s presence, desiring to pay homage, make offerings, serve him personally, and listen to the Dharma; through the Buddha’s spiritual power, these sentient beings experienced no distress or affliction.

Furthermore, there were a hundred koṭis of moons, a hundred koṭis of suns, and a hundred koṭis of oceans, each surrounded by a vast retinue, approaching the place where the Buddha was in order to pay homage, make offerings, serve him personally, and listen to the Dharma.

Furthermore, there was a dragon king named Anavatapta, surrounded by a great retinue, who approached the place where the Buddha was in order to pay homage, make offerings, serve him personally, and listen to the Dharma.

At that time, the World-Honored One’s radiance was brilliant and blazing, eclipsing all the assemblies, just as the white orb of the moon on the fifteenth day, when released from the net of clouds, shines with brilliant and blazing light, eclipsing the circles of all the stars;

even so, even so, the World-Honored One likewise eclipsed the brilliant and blazing radiance of all the Śakras, Brahmās, and World-Protectors, like the brilliant and blazing radiance of Mount Sumeru, King of Mountains, remaining with his body unmoving, unshaken, and breathless, his merit brilliantly blazing.
At that time, the youth Mañjuśrī addressed the bodhisattva Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin, saying:
"Son of the Buddha!
This Tathāgata abides with an unmoving body—neither trembling nor panting."
When he had spoken thus,
the bodhisattva mahāsattva Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin addressed the youthful Mañjuśrī, saying: “Mañjuśrī!
Among this assembly, there are some devas and humans who know that this Tathāgata has gone forth from his home and intends to seek renunciation; some know him dwelling in places of ascetic practice;
among this assembly, some know him approaching the site of enlightenment, and some know him seated at the site of enlightenment.

Within this assembly, some were surrounded by immeasurable and innumerable hosts of Māras; others knew that he had destroyed the Māras. There were immeasurable and innumerable devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, kinnaras, mahoragas, śakras, brahmās, and lokapālas who desired to provide assistance and strength to the supreme Great Caravan Leader. Some knew that after he had realized awakening, Śakra had entreated him; some were Brahmās;
some knew that within this assembly, a Lokapāla had entreated the World-Honored One;
and some knew that the World-Honored One was teaching the *Dāna* (Gift) for our sake.

Within this assembly, some understood that the World-Honored One was teaching us the *śīla* (precepts); some spoke of patience; some spoke of diligence; some spoke of meditative concentration through reflection; some understood that the World-Honored One was teaching us the *prajñāpāramitā* (perfection of wisdom); some spoke of skillful means; some understood that the World-Honored One was teaching us the *praṇidhāna* (vows);
some spoke of the powers (*bala*); and some spoke of *jñāna* (gnosis). Some understood that the World-Honored One was teaching us the *śrāvakayāna*;

some spoke of the *pratyekabuddhayāna*; and some spoke of the *mahāyāna*. Some understood that the World-Honored One was teaching us the dharma of birth among animals; some spoke of birth as hungry ghosts; and some understood that the World-Honored One was teaching us the dharma of birth in the world of Yama.

Some knew that the World-Honored One was teaching us the Dharma for rebirth in the palaces of the Four Great Kings; some were reborn in the Heaven of the Thirty-three; some knew that the World-Honored One was teaching us the Dharma for rebirth in the palaces of the Yāma Heaven; some knew that the World-Honored One was teaching us the Dharma for rebirth in the Tuṣita Heaven; some were reborn in the Nirmāṇarati Heaven; some were reborn in the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven; some were reborn in the Māra Heaven; and some knew that the World-Honored One was teaching us the Dharma for rebirth in the palaces of the Brahmāloka Heaven.
Some were reborn as humans, and some within this assembly knew that the World-Honored One was teaching them that they would become Universal Monarchs (cakravartin).

“Mañjuśrī! Among this assembly, some perceive the Tathāgata as being two *vyāma* tall; some perceive him as one *krośa* tall; some perceive him as two *krośa* tall; some perceive him as half a *yojana* tall; some perceive the height of the Tathāgata’s body as two *yojana*;

some perceive the Tathāgata’s body as ten *yojana*; some among this assembly perceive the Tathāgata’s body as a thousand *yojana*; some perceive the Tathāgata’s body as ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, or a hundred thousand *yojana*; and some perceive the Tathāgata’s body as eighty-four hundred thousand *yojana*.
In this assembly, some perceive the body of the Tathāgata as exceeding hundreds of thousands of *yojanas* in height;
some see it as golden in color; some see it as the color of *vaiḍūrya*, *nīla-maṇi*, or *vajra-maṇi* jewels;
some see it as the color of *indranīla* blue *maṇi* jewels; some see it as the color of great blue *maṇi* jewels; and some see it as the color of fire.
There was the color of the *prabhā-maṇi* jewel; some had the color of the *padmarāga-maṇi* jewel;
some had the color of the *śakrābhilagna-maṇi* jewel of the Tathāgata’s body; some had the color of the *vajraprabhā-maṇi* jewel;
some had the color of the *devaprabhā-maṇi* jewel; and some had the color of the sun and moon.
The color of maṇi jewels: there are those with the color of water-light maṇi jewels;
some with the color of the Tathāgata-praṇidhāna (vow) maṇi jewels; some with the color of the Sovereign King maṇi jewels;
some with the color of the Supreme Radiance maṇi jewels; some with the color of the lion-manes maṇi jewels; or some with...
The color of the maṇi jewels atop the Lion Banner, or the color of the ocean-abiding pure adornment universal-flame-light maṇi jewels. Mañjuśrī!
Furthermore, Mañjuśrī, there are those within this assembly who know the color of the Tathāgata’s wish-fulfilling maṇi jewel;
by abiding in such a color and deportment, they are able to bring sentient beings to spiritual maturity.
Mañjuśrī! Those sentient beings see the Tathāgata abiding in such and such forms and modes of conduct. Mañjuśrī!
Whatever teachings are given to bring sentient beings to maturity, those sentient beings know that the Tathāgata teaches the Dharma in such a way.

Mañjuśrī! Whatever practices cause sentient beings to enter the teaching of the Tathāgata and receive transformation and deliverance, those sentient beings know that the Tathāgata abides in each and every such practice.

“Mañjuśrī! Suppose that in the eastern direction there were immeasurable, innumerable, inconceivable, incomparable, unfathomable, and ineffable worlds, all of which were completely filled with devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, śakras, brahmās, lokapālas, humans, non-humans, and so forth;”

As it was in the eastern direction, so it was in the southern, western, and northern directions; in the southeast, southwest, northwest, and northeast; and likewise in the zenith and nadir—filling immeasurable, innumerable, inconceivable, incomparable, unfathomable, and ineffable worlds with devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, śakras, brahmās, lokapālas, humans, non-humans, and others, like a grove of bamboo, a grove of sugarcane, or a grove of sesame.

Mañjuśrī! If there are sentient beings who, having seen the Tathāgata, attain deliverance, those sentient beings stand at a distance of one fathom before the Tathāgata and see all the various forms and postures of the Tathāgata; those sentient beings who attain deliverance see the Tathāgata standing before them in those respective forms and postures.
Mañjuśrī! Whatever Dharma has been taught shall bring those sentient beings to maturity; they shall each hear such a teaching of the Dharma. Mañjuśrī!

All practices cause those sentient beings to enter the teaching of the Tathāgata; they shall attain maturity through their respective practices, while the Tathāgata abides in the effortless and non-conceptual performance of all the deeds of a Tathāgata, turning them spontaneously.

Mañjuśrī! Just as when the white crescent moon is at midnight, the various sentient beings of Jambudvīpa each perceive the lunar disk before them, yet the lunar disk itself has no discrimination or conceptualization; in this same way, I abide before sentient beings, desiring to cause those sentient beings to know my lunar disk.
Mañjuśrī! However, the lunar disc is effortless and non-conceptual; therefore, this matter of form thus manifests, by virtue of its unique quality (asādhāraṇadharma), in such and such a way.
The Flower Ornament Scripture on Entering the Inconceivable Realm of the Tathāgata’s Virtue and Wisdom, Volume One;
The Flower Ornament Scripture on Entering the Inconceivable Realm of the Tathāgata’s Virtue and Wisdom, Volume Two.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta of India during the Sui Dynasty: "Mañjuśrī!
When the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha is amidst the assembly, all those sentient beings see the Tathāgata standing before them."

The Tathāgata is likewise without conceptualization or discursive differentiation; yet, I abide before sentient beings, desiring that they know the Tathāgata abides before them. Nevertheless, according to those sentient beings who are to be transformed and delivered, each perceives the Tathāgata as abiding before them.
Why is this? Because it is associated with the unique qualities (āveṇika-dharma), Mañjuśrī!

For example, according to the ripening power of the inferior, middling, or superior karma of sentient beings, there arise corresponding inferior, middling, or superior formations that bring sentient beings into existence. Yet these formations are without discrimination or conceptual differentiation; nevertheless, because they are effortless and non-conceptual, the activities of the inferior, middling, and superior formations proceed spontaneously.

"So it is, so it is, Mañjuśrī! According to the power of the ripening of the inferior, middling, and superior karma of sentient beings, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha likewise appears to sentient beings as inferior, middling, and superior."
Mañjuśrī! The Tathāgata is likewise without conceptualization or discursive differentiation; yet, because he is without effort and without conceptualization, the Tathāgata functions in this manner.
“Mañjuśrī! For example, just as a genuine sphāṭika mani-jewel appears in various colors according to the variety of cloths [upon which it rests], Mañjuśrī!”
If the *sphāṭika-maṇi* jewel is placed upon a yellow garment, the *sphāṭika-maṇi* jewel immediately becomes yellow;
if placed upon a red garment, the *sphāṭika-maṇi* jewel immediately becomes red;
if placed upon a blue garment, the *sphāṭika-maṇi* jewel immediately becomes blue.
In this way, whatever kind of form it is placed upon, it produces a form corresponding to that very one. Mañjuśrī,
the *prajñā-kāmaṇi* jewel is likewise without conceptualization or discursive differentiation.
"So it is, so it is, Mañjuśrī! The Tathāgata assumes various forms according to the forms of sentient beings. Mañjuśrī!"
If sentient beings are to be transformed and delivered by the appearance of the golden body of the Tathāgata, they shall see the golden body of the Tathāgata;
if sentient beings are to be transformed and delivered by the color of the Vaiḍūryanirbhāsa-maṇi jewel, they shall see the color of the Vaiḍūryanirbhāsa-maṇi jewel;
if sentient beings are to be transformed and delivered by the color of pearls, they shall see the Tathāgata in the color of pearls.

If there are sentient beings who are to be transformed and delivered through the color of the celestial Indra-blue maṇi jewel, they shall see the Tathāgata as having the color of the celestial Indra-blue maṇi jewel.
Mañjuśrī! If there are sentient beings who are to be converted by the color of the great blue maṇi jewel, they shall see the Tathāgata as having the color of the great blue maṇi jewel;

if there are sentient beings who are to be converted by the color of the *sarvaratnābhāsasamudgata* (all-light-select) maṇi jewel, they shall see the Tathāgata as having the color of the *sarvaratnābhāsasamudgata* maṇi jewel.

If there are sentient beings who are to be converted by the color of the ocean-abiding pure-adornment universal-flame-light maṇi jewel, they shall see the Tathāgata as having the color of the ocean-abiding pure-adornment universal-flame-light maṇi jewel;
if there are sentient beings who are to be converted by the color of the lion-manes maṇi jewel, they shall see the Tathāgata as having the color of the lion-manes maṇi jewel;
if there are sentient beings who are to be converted by the color of the lion-banner-top maṇi jewel, they shall see the Tathāgata as having the color of the lion-banner-top maṇi jewel.
Mañjuśrī! If sentient beings are to be transformed and delivered by means of the color of the lightning-lamp maṇi jewel, they shall see the Tathāgata with the color of the lightning-lamp maṇi jewel;
if sentient beings are to be transformed and delivered by means of the color of the water-purifying maṇi jewel, they shall see the Tathāgata with the color of the water-purifying maṇi jewel.
Mañjuśrī! Thus, if those who are to be converted by the form of Brahmā, Śakra, or the World-Protectors (Lokapālas) should see the Tathāgata in the form of Brahmā, Śakra, or the World-Protectors;

and even among those born in the realms of hell-beings, animals, hungry ghosts, or the world of Yama—whatever kind of beings are born there, if they are to be converted by whatever physical form or majestic demeanor, they shall see the Tathāgata with such a physical form and such a majestic demeanor.

Likewise, whether born from eggs, from a womb, from moisture, or by transformation; whether possessing form or being formless; whether with perception, without perception, or neither with nor without perception—whatever physical form or physical demeanor may be used to bring them to spiritual transformation and deliverance, the Tathāgata shall manifest such a physical form and physical demeanor for them to behold.
Yet the Tathāgata is without discrimination and without conceptual differentiation; he desires that these beings see my golden color and not the color of vaidūrya-blue;
that these beings see my vaidūrya-blue color and not the color of the celestial king’s blue maṇi-jewel;
and that these beings see my celestial king’s blue maṇi-jewel color and not the color of the great blue maṇi-jewel.
These sentient beings see my color as the great blue maṇi jewel, but do not see the color of the *sarvaratnābhāsavyūha* maṇi jewel;
these sentient beings see my color as the *sarvaratnābhāsavyūha* maṇi jewel, but do not see the color of the *vaśavarti-rāja* maṇi jewel;
these sentient beings see my color as the *vaśavarti-rāja* maṇi jewel, but do not see the color of the *sāgaranivāsa-vyūha-viśuddha-samantaprabhāsa* maṇi jewel.
These sentient beings see me as having the color of the ocean-dwelling pure-adornment universal-flame-light maṇi-jewel, and do not see me as having the color of the lion-maned maṇi-jewel;
these sentient beings see me as having the color of the lion-maned maṇi-jewel, and do not see me as having the color of the lion-banner-top maṇi-jewel.

In this way, the Tathāgata is likewise without discrimination and without diverse discrimination; yet, because he is without effort and without discrimination, such activities of various forms proceed.
“Mañjuśrī! For example, wherever the sovereign king-maṇi jewel originates, there iron or iron implements do not arise. Mañjuśrī!”
That Sovereign King is free from discriminatory thoughts; he does not think:
"In the place where I am born, may there be no iron, nor any tools made of iron."
"Mañjuśrī! Wherever the sovereign king maṇi jewel originates, there iron or iron implements do not arise; it is just so, it is just so."

Mañjuśrī! In all those buddha-fields where the Tathāgata is born, there are no non-Buddhists such as the Śrāvakas, Parivrājakas, or Nirgranthas; there, no evil deeds arise; there, no disturbances arise; there, no acts of immediate retribution arise; there, the ten unwholesome paths of action do not arise; there, no kings whose teachings contradict the Dharma arise; there, the light of the sun and moon does not arise; there, the light of the Brahmas, Śakras, and Lokapālas does not arise; there, the light of jewels or fire does not arise; and there, no calculations of *muhūrta*, half-*muhūrta*, months, fortnights, or years arise.
Mañjuśrī! This is except for the sustaining power of the Tathāgata, which exists for the sake of maturing sentient beings. Mañjuśrī!

The Tathāgata likewise has no conceptualization and no discursive differentiation; nevertheless, in accordance with sentient beings, these matters proceed through effortlessness and non-conceptualization. "Mañjuśrī!..."

For example, whatever is touched by the radiance of a great sapphire mani jewel all takes on the color of that great sapphire mani jewel, yet the great sapphire mani jewel has no conceptual thought of discrimination.

"So it is, so it is, Mañjuśrī! Those who are touched by the light of the Tathāgata’s intentional focus all manifest as the form of omniscience, yet the Tathāgata remains without conceptualization or discursive differentiation."
Mañjuśrī! Nevertheless, these matters proceed for the Tathāgata through effortlessness and non-conceptuality. Mañjuśrī!

For example, suppose there were a well-crafted great Vaiḍūrya maṇi jewel; wherever it is placed among various ornaments—whether among foot ornaments or head ornaments—it would radiate the most intense light within each respective ornament, and those ornaments themselves would also radiate the most intense light, all due to the power of that Vaiḍūrya maṇi jewel. It is just so, it is just so.

Mañjuśrī! In whatever modes of conduct, deportment, or dwellings the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha abides, and in whatever manner he dwells within those various conducts, he illuminates them most intensely, and those conducts themselves are also most intensely illuminated; this is due to the majestic power of that Tathāgata.

Mañjuśrī! The Tathāgata is likewise without conceptualization or discursive differentiation; nevertheless, because the Tathāgata acts without effort and without conceptualization, these matters proceed.
“Mañjuśrī! Just as, by virtue of the earth’s support and the earth’s sustaining power, all grasses, trees, medicinal herbs, forests, and seeds grow and expand.”
Mañjuśrī! That ground is free from conceptual thought; yet, because it is non-conceptual through effortlessness, these phenomena proceed. It is so, Mañjuśrī, it is so.

By virtue of the Tathāgata’s reliance and by virtue of the Tathāgata’s sustaining power, the various roots of goodness of all sentient beings increase and expand; yet the Tathāgata is without conceptualization or discursive differentiation. Nevertheless, through his effortless and non-conceptual state, these matters proceed.

“Mañjuśrī! It is like a mass of clouds that, having covered all the earth, pours down great rain everywhere upon various grasses, trees, medicinal herbs, and forests. Although that water is of a single taste, it causes the various grasses, trees, medicinal herbs, and forests to grow; yet in their various locations, that water abides with various tastes and various colors.”
Mañjuśrī! That cloud is free from conceptual thought; yet, because it is effortless and non-conceptual, these things proceed in such and such a manner.

Mañjuśrī! The Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, having pervaded and filled the worlds of the ten directions with clouds of Buddha-bodies, rains down various Dharma-showers everywhere upon the various roots of goodness accumulated by sentient beings, their various aspirations, their various internal faiths and understandings, and their various abodes of liberation. By means of these various Dharma-showers, according to their respective capacities and strengths, he causes their roots of goodness to increase—namely, the roots of goodness accumulated by sentient beings, their aspirations, their internal faith and understanding, and their individual roots of goodness, aspirations, internal faith, and abodes of liberation.

Mañjuśrī! The Tathāgata is likewise without conceptualization or discursive differentiation; yet, for the sake of these sentient beings, I cultivate their roots of goodness so that they may attain the wisdom of śrāvakas;
and for the sake of these sentient beings, I cultivate their roots of goodness so that they may attain the wisdom of pratyekabuddhas.
For the sake of these sentient beings, I increase their roots of goodness so that they may attain the wisdom of a Buddha;
for the sake of these sentient beings, I increase their roots of goodness so that they may be born in the palaces of the Four Great Heavenly Kings;
for the sake of these, I increase their roots of goodness so that they may be born in the palaces of the Thirty-three Heavens.

Thus it is briefly stated, extending even to the Yāma, Tuṣita, Nirmāṇarati, and Paranirmita-vaśavartin [heavens], as well as the Brahmakāyika, Brahmapurohita, Parīttābha, Apramāṇābha, Ābhāsvara, Parīttaśubha, Apramāṇaśubha, Śubhakṛtsna, Bṛhatphala, Puṇyaprasava, Śuddhāvāsa, and Akaniṣṭha [realms].

Mañjuśrī! The Tathāgata does not make such discriminations as, "I shall cause these sentient beings to increase their roots of goodness so that they will be born in various royal states," or "I shall cause these sentient beings to increase their roots of goodness so that they will be born in various human states."
He causes these sentient beings to increase their roots of goodness so that they shall be born in various states of mastery.
Mañjuśrī! Even the Tathāgata is without conceptualization and without discursive differentiation.

Mañjuśrī! Nevertheless, because the Tathāgata is without effort and without conceptual discrimination, he acts in accordance with the vows, inner faith and understanding, and the accumulation of roots of goodness of sentient beings; such various types of phenomena thus proceed.
Yet the Tathāgata remains detached from all these bases, free from any conceptual discrimination.

“Mañjuśrī! For example, when the orb of the sun rises, it successively emits countless hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of rays of light, dispelling all the darkness within Jambudvīpa. Yet that solar orb has no conceptualization and no discursive differentiation; nevertheless, through its effortless and non-conceptual nature, these activities proceed.”

"So it is, so it is, Mañjuśrī! When the sun-disk of the Tathāgata rises, it sequentially emits countless hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of rays of wisdom, dispelling the darkness created by all views, except for those instances where the Buddha intentionally maintains his presence in order to bring sentient beings to maturity."

Mañjuśrī, the Tathāgata is likewise without conceptual discrimination; he thinks, "I shall now shatter the perception of things for the sake of sentient beings," or "I shall shatter the perception of things. Mañjuśrī!
Nevertheless, because the Tathāgata is without effort and without conceptual discrimination, such categories of phenomena as these proceed.
Mañjuśrī! The Tathāgata is equanimous toward all objects; he possesses no conceptual discrimination.
“Mañjuśrī! For example, it is like a magical creation produced by a magician who manifests various things; because it is effortless and non-conceptual, it divides itself into various bodies.”

Mañjuśrī! That which is conjured by illusion cannot be said to arise or cease; it is without letters and without sound, without location and without substance, without perception and without thought, without duality and without activity, and without equal and without counterpart.
Mañjuśrī! However, that which is emanated by illusion appears as various phenomena because of the illusionist; it does so without effort and without conceptual discrimination.
"So it is, so it is, Mañjuśrī! The Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, in accordance with sentient beings, manifests various modes of conduct, dignified postures, and spheres of activity."
Mañjuśrī! That Tathāgata is ineffable;

he is neither born nor extinguished; he is without letters or sounds; he has no location or spatial dimension and possesses no substantial entity; he is without conceptualization or volition; he is non-dual and without activity; he is equal to the dharma-realm and is without counterpart.
“Mañjuśrī! For example, because of the sun’s movement around Mount Meru, the king of mountains, among the sentient beings of the four great continents,
some see it when it is rising, some see it when it is setting, some see it when it is high in the sky, or some— ”

Regarding the knowledge of the time for descending [into the womb], there are those who know it at midnight, some at midday, and others who know it at the first striking of the drum when the sun rises.
In that country, a single day is divided into four parts; when one part has elapsed, the drum is struck as a signal.
This refers to the first striking of the drum during these four divisions, or the time for descending.
When the drum is first struck, it may be struck when the day is still remaining, or it may be struck when the night is still remaining;

thus, regarding the solar disk, the sentient beings within the four great continents each perceive it differently. Yet the solar disk itself has no discrimination nor any conceptual differentiation; nevertheless, due to the wandering of the world-system, the four continents— [...]* *Note:

The provided source text appears to be a fragment of a larger passage concerning the perception of the sun by beings in the four continents (caturdvīpa) despite the sun's lack of inherent discrimination.*
Within the realm, it manifests various phenomena because it is effortless and non-conceptual.
Thus it is, thus it is, Mañjuśrī!

Among this assembly, there are sentient beings who know that the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, is about to realize awakening; some know he is about to enter parinirvāṇa; some know that the World-Honored One has already realized awakening; some in this assembly know that the World-Honored One has already entered parinirvāṇa; some know it has been ten years since the World-Honored One realized awakening; some know it has been ten thousand years since the World-Honored One entered parinirvāṇa; some know it is the time when the World-Honored One’s teaching is in its pure height; some know it is the time when the World-Honored One’s teaching is fading away; some know it has been ten, twenty, thirty, or forty years since the World-Honored One began preaching the Dharma; and some know it has been ten, twenty, thirty, or forty *koṭi-nayuta-śata-sahasra* kalpas since the World-Honored One entered parinirvāṇa.
Mañjuśrī! There may be gods and humans who know that the Blessed One Śākyamuni attained awakening incalculable upon incalculable eons ago, Mañjuśrī!
The Tathāgata likewise has neither discrimination nor conceptual differentiation.
Mañjuśrī, nevertheless,
because the Tathāgata is effortless and non-conceptual, he acts in accordance with the various types of beings that exist.

“Mañjuśrī! For example, when a great wind-circle blows upon Jambudvīpa, all its grasses, trees, medicinal forests, and leaves shake, shaking again and again; they are disordered, becoming disordered again and again. Some leaves dip low in the east and rise high in the west; some leaves dip low in the west and rise high in the east; some leaves rise at the edges and dip low in the center; others rise in the north and dip low in the south. Yet these grasses, trees, medicinal forests, and leaves have no discrimination; nevertheless, by following the wind-circle, their various functions proceed.”

"So it is, so it is, Mañjuśrī! The Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, is likewise without conceptualization or discursive differentiation; yet, for the sake of sentient beings, throughout every moment of time, he constantly manifests such incalculable activities, modes of conduct, and engagements with objects."

Mañjuśrī! To whatever extent sentient beings direct their thoughts toward the Tathāgata as an object of focus, for that many eons shall they sever and turn away from all rebirths in the realms of hell-beings, animals, hungry ghosts, and the world of Yama.
Mañjuśrī! In this way, the Tathāgata is endowed with the immeasurable. Mañjuśrī!

Even if one were able to focus the mind upon the Tathāgata as a single object of perception for immeasurable, incalculable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of *koṭi-nayuta* kalpas, remaining in inconceivable liberations and *samādhis*, a bodhisattva mahāsattva could not reach the limit of that [Tathāgata’s] merit.

“Mañjuśrī! It is like the sun rising from the great ocean and appearing in the realm of space; it emits countless hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of rays, manifesting itself within villages, cities, kingdoms, and royal capitals, thereby dispelling darkness and drying up turbid mud. It causes all grasses, trees, medicinal forests, and herbs to grow, brings various medicines to maturity, and initiates all manner of activities. Simultaneously, its reflection reaches all rivers, ponds, and lakes, yet its dwelling place remains unmoving.”
Mañjuśrī! The solar disc is likewise without conceptualization or discursive differentiation; yet, by virtue of being effortless and non-conceptual, such phenomena as these proceed in this manner.

"So it is, so it is, Mañjuśrī! The Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, having arisen from the ocean of existence, emerges and dwells in the realm of space. He radiates countless hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of flames of wisdom throughout the worlds of the ten directions, manifesting them everywhere. For the sake of all sentient beings, he shatters and disperses the cataracts of the darkness of ignorance, dries up the turbid mud of the afflictions, causes all roots of goodness to grow, brings the accumulations of roots of goodness to maturity, and initiates all gateways of goodness; yet at one and the same time, while these activities proceed, he remains unmoving in his dwelling place."
Mañjuśrī! The Tathāgata is likewise without conceptualization or discursive differentiation; yet, because he is effortless and non-conceptual, such phenomena as these proceed in this manner.
“Mañjuśrī! Suppose there were sons or daughters of good family who, for as many days as there are atoms in all the worlds of the ten directions,
offered celestial food of a hundred flavors and celestial garments every day to all the Buddhas and their assemblies of śrāvakas.”
When giving in this manner, one gives for as many eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River;
after those [Tathāgatas] have entered parinirvāṇa, for each and every Tathāgata, one constructs throughout the worlds of the ten directions, within each individual world,
stūpas equal in number to the atoms of all the worlds of the ten directions, with bodies made of Jambūnada gold.
It was interspersed with electric lamps and maṇi jewels; it was surrounded by railings made of various selected maṇi jewels;
it was adorned with suspended maṇi beads; banners, flags, and canopies were erected; it was covered above with nets of bells;
it was anointed with the fragrance of great snake-secure sandalwood (mahāuraga-dṛḍha-candana); it was covered above with nets of maṇis; those... saha... [continued].
Subhūti, suppose one were to take canopies as numerous as the measure of a trichiliocosm, along with clouds of banners, clouds of incense,
clouds of sovereign *maṇi* jewels, and clouds of wish-fulfilling *maṇi* jewels, scattering them again and again at three times each day;
and suppose one were to perform such offerings for as many eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River.
Furthermore, Mañjuśrī, there are other immeasurable and incalculable sentient beings whom he also instructs to abide in such offerings. Mañjuśrī!

If there are other sons or daughters of good family who even believe and resolve upon this *Dharmaparyāya on Entering the Inconceivable Realm of the Tathāgata’s Qualities*, the merit produced by them will exceed that [of the former] by incalculable proportions.
“Mañjuśrī! A bodhisattva who has faith and understanding in this Dharma-fundamental shall fulfill immeasurable,
incalculable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of pāramitās, and shall transcend immeasurable, incalculable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas.”
O son of noble family, you shall, for immeasurable, incalculable, hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of *kalpas*, turn your back upon [samsara];
you should know that you shall sport with immeasurable, incalculable, hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas;
you shall shatter the immeasurable, incalculable mountains of pride; you shall topple the immeasurable, incalculable banners of stinginess and envy; and you shall dry up...
One shall cross the immeasurable and incalculable rivers of craving; one shall cross the immeasurable and incalculable oceans of birth and death;
one shall sever the immeasurable and incalculable snares of Māra; one shall obstruct the power of the sun, moon, Śakra, Brahmā, and the World-Protectors;
and traveling from buddha-field to buddha-field, one shall provide protection and refuge.
Sentient beings born in the realms of Naraka, Preta, Piśāca, and Yama will encounter all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas;
they shall attain the Samādhi of the Ocean Seal (Sāgaramudrā-samādhi),
they shall attain the Samādhi named Entering the Equality of All Dharmas, and they shall attain the Samādhi named Sovereign Transformation of All Dharmas.
This stage shall be named the Samādhi Adorned with All Marks; it shall be named the Samādhi Born from Jewels;
it shall be named the Samādhi Producing Joy; it shall be named the Samādhi Adorned with Lotuses;
it shall be named the Samādhi of the Treasury of Space; and it shall be named the Samādhi Accordant with All Worlds.
When practicing samādhi, it shall be named the Samādhi of the White Flower of the True Dharma;
it shall be named the Samādhi of Sovereign Transformation of the Realm; it shall be named the Samādhi of Great Yawning;
it shall be named the Samādhi of Sovereign Transformation of the Mind of Emptiness; and it shall be named the Samādhi of the Lion’s Yawn.
This stage shall be named the Sun-Lamp Samādhi; it shall be named the Boundless Whirlpool Samādhi;
it shall be named the Steep Descent and Forward Movement Samādhi; it shall be named the Vajra-Wheel Samādhi;
it shall be named the Vajra-Banner Samādhi; and it shall be named Like a Vajra.
Maitreya, it shall be named the Vajra-Edge Samādhi; it shall be named the Earth-Sustaining Samādhi;
it shall be named the Meru-Lamp Samādhi; it shall be named the Samādhi of Sovereign Transformation of the Minds of All Sentient Beings;
and it shall be named the Samādhi of Emergence from the Spheres of Activity of All Sentient Beings.
It shall be named the Merudhvaja Samādhi; it shall be named the Ratnakośa Samādhi;
it shall be named the Cittavaśavartin Samādhi; it shall be named the Gūḍhopāya Samādhi;
it shall be named the Citraraśmipratibhāna Samādhi; and it shall be named the Avalokita Samādhi.

One shall attain the samādhi named "Contemplating All Dharmas," one shall attain the samādhi named "Sportive Play," one shall attain the samādhi named "Not Delighting in Superior Knowledges and Supernatural Powers," one shall attain the samādhi named "Shattering the Māra-Wheel," one shall attain the samādhi named "Manifesting All Forms," and one shall attain...
It shall be named the Samādhi that Greatly Benefits All Forms; it shall be named the Samādhi of Contemplating the Body;
it shall be named the Samādhi of the Lord of Faithful Practice; it shall be named the Samādhi of the Lamp of Wisdom;
it shall be named the Samādhi of the Manifest Lamp of Awakening; it shall be named the Samādhi of Explaining Specific Deficiencies; and it shall be attained...
It shall be named the Samādhi of Entering All Marks and Merit; it shall be named the Samādhi of Resolute Practice of All Dharmas;
it shall be named the Samādhi of Tranquil and Resolute Supernormal Powers; it shall be named the Samādhi of Valiant Conduct;
it shall be named the Samādhi of the Deep Ocean Waves of Fearlessness; and it shall be like...
With these as their foremost, they shall attain incalculable hundreds of thousands of millions (*koṭi*) and billions (*nayuta*) of samādhis.

They shall attain the *dhāraṇī* of the manifestation of the infinite color of the Buddha-body; they shall attain the *dhāraṇī* named Sovereign of Wisdom (*jñānendra*); they shall attain the *dhāraṇī* named Pure Resounding Voice; they shall attain the *dhāraṇī* named Inexhaustible Casket; they shall attain the *dhāraṇī* named Boundless Abyss; they shall attain the *dhāraṇī* named Ocean Seal (*sāgaramudrā*); they shall attain the *dhāraṇī* named Lotus Ornamentation; they shall attain the *dhāraṇī* named Entry into the Gate of Non-attachment; they shall attain the *dhāraṇī* named Right Determination (*samyak-niyata*); they shall attain the *dhāraṇī* named Sustaining the Buddha’s Necklace. With these as their foremost, they shall attain incalculable hundreds of thousands of millions and billions of such *dhāraṇīs*.

One shall accordingly attain supremacy over all conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*); one shall accordingly attain non-dependent wisdom regarding all dharmas; one shall accordingly attain the severance of all doubts; one shall accordingly attain hundreds of thousands of incalculable Buddha-playful manifestations (*vikrīḍita*); and one shall accordingly attain skillfulness that excels the conduct of all sentient beings.
“Mañjuśrī, it is just as Mount Meru,
the king of mountains, outshines all other mountains with its blazing radiance.
In this very way, in this very way, Mañjuśrī!”
"In this fundamental teaching, the bodhisattvas who possess faith and understanding outshine all sentient beings, for the light of their various roots of goodness blazes and shines brilliantly.
At that time, the youth Mañjuśrī addressed the bodhisattva mahāsattva Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin, saying:
"O Son of the Buddha!..."
"Furthermore, among those with faith and understanding who possess other superior dharmas, will there be bodhisattvas who shall likewise attain such other superior merits?
When he had spoken thus,
the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Āvaraṇavikiraṇa addressed the youth Mañjuśrī, saying:
“Mañjuśrī! There are five qualities through which a bodhisattva who has faith and understanding shall attain such distinguished and superior merits.
What are these five?

All phenomena are without opposition, without arising, and without cessation, and are ineffable; one should have faith and understanding in this way. Beyond the most minute atoms of Jambudvīpa lie the Tathāgata’s modes of conduct, his deportment, and his spheres of activity; they are effortless and non-conceptual, constantly unfolding in every moment of thought—one should have faith and understanding in this way.

One should believe and understand that the Blessed One Śākyamuni has already attained awakening throughout as many eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River, while performing deeds within his perpetual assemblies to bring sentient beings to maturity.

From the time he received the prediction from Dīpaṃkara Buddha until his realization of awakening, all the bodhisattva practices performed during that interval were fully realized and manifested by the Blessed One Śākyamuni throughout kalpas equal in duration to the entire scope of a Buddha’s domain; one should have faith and understanding in this way.

Regarding the execution of Śākyamuni, which was a manifestation of his deeds for the sake of maturing sentient beings: one should have such faith and understanding that the World-Honored One, Śākyamuni, manifested his attainment of awakening throughout kalpas equal in duration to the entirety of the Buddha-realm.
Mañjuśrī! These five kinds of bodhisattvas with resolute belief shall attain such distinct and superior merits. Mañjuśrī!

If there were sons or daughters of good family who were to give to Arhats established in the eight liberations—equal in number to the atoms of all worlds—divine food of a hundred flavors, and daily offer divine garments, and were to give in this manner for as many eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River; [the merit of one who hears this Dharma would be greater than that].

Mañjuśrī! If there is a son of good family or a daughter of good family who gives a single meal to a single pratyekabuddha for one day, this merit surpasses that [previous merit] by an incalculable number of times.

Mañjuśrī! If there are sons of good family or daughters of good family who construct vihāras— what the old translations call "monasteries"— as numerous as the atoms in the worlds of the ten directions,
wherein each world is composed of Jambūnada gold and interspersed with lightning-lamp maṇi jewels;

It was surrounded by railings of *cintāmaṇi* jewels that select all radiances, fashioned from strings of *maṇi* jewels; it was adorned with established canopies, banners, and pennants, with curtains made of bell-nets, and floors plastered with firm, snake-like sandalwood;
it was covered above by sovereign *maṇi* jewels, and its pillars were made of ocean-abiding, pure, and universally radiant *maṇi* jewels.
He connected nets of *śīrṣaka-sūmaṇi* jewels to form a covering over them;
he used *śīrṣadhvaja-vijaya-maṇi* jewels as defensive turrets;
and for the pratyekabuddhas, he hung bundles of silk streamers upon the battlements and windows, numbering in the thousands beyond calculation.

For the sake of those pratyekabuddhas, he daily bestowed upon them celestial food of a hundred flavors and also bestowed celestial garments; he gave such gifts for as many kalpas as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River.

Mañjuśrī! If a son of good family or a daughter of good family hears the voice of the Buddha, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata, the merit arising from this exceeds that [previous merit] by incalculable degrees; how much more so if they see the Tathāgata at a place where he has been depicted in a painting or fashioned from clay—the merit arising from this exceeds that by incalculable degrees.

How much more so if they offer lamps, burn incense, apply fragrant ointments, or present flowers, or even other various kinds of ritual implements—the merit arising from this exceeds that by incalculable degrees. How much more so if, for the sake of the Tathāgata, they observe a single precept for a single day—the merit arising from this exceeds that by incalculable degrees.
“Mañjuśrī! If a son of good family or a daughter of good family were to daily provide divine food of a hundred flavors to as many Tathāgatas,
bodhisattvas, and assemblies of śrāvakas as there are atoms in the worlds of the ten directions, and furthermore— ”
One gives divine garments; giving in this manner for as many eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River,
one constructs for each and every Tathāgata after their parinirvāṇa a stūpa equal in number to the atoms within the worlds of the ten directions,
with each stūpa being as vast as the four continents and complete with all various marks.
Its base is composed of Jambūnada gold, adorned with interlaced lightning-bright maṇi jewels;
it is surrounded by railings of various radiant *cintāmaṇi* gems, decorated with bundles of precious pearls, and established with various canopies,
banners, and streamers, with nets of bells forming a curtain, winding like a serpent.
They are firmly plastered with sandalwood paste and covered above with sovereign *maṇi* jewels;

those *stūpas* are daily honored by clouds of parasols, banners, jewel-clouds, music-clouds, garland-clouds, lion-banner-victorious-moon-clouds, and divine manifestations, equal in measure to a trichiliocosm.
Clouds of drum music and song were scattered above them;
though they were scattered again and again, they did not have faith in or understand this Dharma-fundament, Mañjuśrī!

If there is a son of good family or a daughter of good family who, having gained faith and understanding in this *dharmamūla* called "Entering the Inconceivable Sphere of the Tathāgata’s Merit and Wisdom," gives even a single morsel of food to a being in the realm of animals, this merit surpasses that [previous merit] by an incalculable number of times.
Mañjuśrī! If there is a bodhisattva who has faith and understanding in this sūtra and makes offerings to the Tathāgata as described in this sūtra;

and if there is another bodhisattva who, upon seeing that bodhisattva who has faith and understanding in this sūtra, forms this thought: "This one has faith and understands this sūtra"—and having formed such a thought, attains great joy and pure faith, rises from his seat, joins his palms in prostration, and according to his capacity and strength, receives and makes offerings to him—this latter person’s merit shall surpass that of the former by incalculable degrees, for he shall attain the wisdom of a Buddha.

When the Buddha had spoken these words, those bhikṣus, as well as the bodhisattvas, devas, humans, asuras, gandharvas, and other beings in the world, rejoiced in what the Buddha had taught and practiced it accordingly.
The Sutra on Entering the Inconceivable Realm of the Tathāgata’s Virtue and Wisdom, Scroll Lower.
